headline: Reported Ukrainian drone strikes hit Omsk petrochemical plant and warehouse in Siberia
body:
What happened: Monitoring channels reported that Ukraine struck several targets in Omsk, a Russian city roughly 2,500 kilometres from the Ukrainian border, on October 24. A fire was said to have broken out at the Omsky Kauchuk petrochemical plant, a major Russian producer of synthetic rubber and a fuel additive, and an Ozon warehouse was reportedly hit too. Omsk's regional governor confirmed a drone attack on a logistics hub and said staff were evacuated. The Kyiv Independent could not immediately verify these reports.

Reported by: Kyiv Independent. Also covered by Reuters, Ukrainska Pravda, Meduza.

body:

The claim was relayed by the group's Al-Masirah television channel. The report comes as both sides in the Hodeidah fighting continue to carry out strikes, and the casualty figures are the Houthis' account, which could not be independently verified in this report.

headline: Missile strike lands near Aden airport after governor leaves
body:
What happened: A ballistic missile struck near Aden International Airport in Yemen shortly after Governor Abdulrahman Sheikh had left the site during an inspection tour. Sheikh, who is also Yemen's minister of state, told Asharq Al-Awsat he was unharmed and that the runway rehabilitation, roughly 70 to 80 percent complete, was funded by a Saudi programme. He said his tour continued and that security agencies had uncovered several Houthi sleeper cells in Aden and other provinces.

Sheikh also described ongoing shortages of cooking gas, electricity and medicines in the city, and credited Saudi and King Salman aid bodies with help on supplies.

Reported by: Xinhua. Also covered by Asharq Al-Awsat, China Daily.

headline: Starlink speeds restored for Ukraine after week-long military disruption
body:
What happened: Ukraine's Defense Ministry said Starlink and its military counterpart Starshield are again running at high speeds, following more than a week of restrictions that disrupted frontline operations. The limits, which began around October 14, reportedly stopped Ukrainian units from intercepting Russian attack drones and forced some drone missions to be cancelled. The ministry did not say whether service had been fully restored, and the system's maximum speeds are not publicly disclosed.

The disruption came as tensions rose between Washington and Kyiv over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries, and after a US deal to buy Russian diesel. Responsibility is disputed: some reports blame the White House, others say SpaceX chief Elon Musk ordered the slowdown, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the decisions were commercial. Congress has called for an investigation.

Reported by: Jerusalem Post. Also covered by Politico Europe, Ukrainska Pravda, Kyiv Independent, Taipei Times.

headline: ICC deputy prosecutor says court's work continues despite new US sanctions
body:
What happened: Nazhat Shameem Khan, who is co-leading the International Criminal Court's office until a new chief prosecutor is named, told the Guardian that US sanctions are starting to affect some staff, particularly with banking. She said the court has not cut any investigations because of them, and that work on the Gaza war and other cases has advanced, though secret court orders mean little can be disclosed. The sanctions were announced by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who gave the court six months to respond to US concerns.

The court is moving its software away from Microsoft to European alternatives and negotiating with service providers on banking and health insurance. Khan also said the court's former chief prosecutor, Karim Khan, who denies misconduct allegations, was removed in July.

Reported by: The Guardian

headline: Israeli strikes kill Palestinians in Gaza as food shortages deepen
body:
What happened: Israeli attacks across Gaza killed four Palestinians, including a young girl, over a 24-hour period, according to reports cited in the article. A strike on a vehicle in Gaza City's Tal al-Hawa area killed one person, and a man on a bicycle was killed in Khan Younis. Israeli forces are also reported to be expanding control over more territory in the enclave, with the article saying nearly two-thirds of Gaza is under Israeli military control or access restrictions.

The article also warns that shortages of fresh food and staples are worsening after Israeli restrictions on goods and funding cuts to aid operations. A rights group cited in the piece warned of another possible famine, while the World Food Programme said it had cut food aid by a third.

Reported by: The New Arab. Also covered by Middle East Eye, Euronews, Africanews, Asharq Al-Awsat.

Kyiv had complained that the limits, which it said caused drones to lose contact at high speeds, were imposed at the request of US President Donald Trump, a claim Trump denied before saying billionaire Elon Musk had restored the service. headline: Israeli forces raze Hebron neighbourhood after deadly checkpoint attack
body:
What happened: Israeli troops have flattened a large part of the Ein Deir Baha district in Hebron, in the occupied West Bank, after two gunmen attacked a military checkpoint outside the city on Friday. Two Israeli soldiers and both attackers died in the gunfight. Local Palestinian officials say around 1,500 people have been forced from their homes, and the whole city of 250,000 has been cut off by checkpoints. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich vowed a harsh response ahead of Israeli elections in four days. The Israeli army had not yet responded to requests for comment on the demolitions.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by The Guardian, France 24, Le Monde, Middle East Eye.

A Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two ballistic missiles aimed at the Saudi cities of Taif and Yanbu, and the fighting between the two sides was continuing. headline: Amnesty urges accountability for Gaza killings and warns of humanitarian crisis
body:
What happened: Amnesty International has called on the international community to hold Israel accountable for deaths and humanitarian conditions in Gaza more than a year after a ceasefire agreement. The rights group said over 1,400 people have been killed by Israeli forces since the truce, nearly two million people still need shelter, no hospital is fully operating, and 1.4 million face crisis-level hunger. It argued that any recovery plan for Gaza must rest on international law, justice and victims' rights. Amnesty also criticised what it called a persistent failure to make Israel comply with binding orders from the International Court of Justice.

Reported by: Middle East Eye. Also covered by France 24.

headline: Oil nears five-month high as Hormuz tanker attacks and stalled talks grow
body:
What happened: Oil prices rose toward their highest level in five months as attacks on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz increased and efforts to end the US-Israel war on Iran stalled. Brent crude climbed above $110 a barrel on Wednesday. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they struck several tankers, which Washington disputed. The Houthis have also seized territory in Yemen near the Bab al-Mandeb chokepoint, while the world's emergency oil stocks have fallen to their lowest levels in decades.

Analysts warn that usable reserves outside China are limited, with Japan holding nearly half of what remains. A full closure of Hormuz and Houthi blockades could cut Middle Eastern crude supply sharply.

Reported by: AP. Also covered by Reuters, Al Jazeera, The Guardian, France 24.

headline: Oil slick from struck tanker spreads along UAE coast, beaches closed
body:
What happened: An oil slick from a tanker damaged near the Strait of Hormuz has spread along the United Arab Emirates coastline, leading to the closure of some beaches and coastal areas. The vessel, identified by BBC Verify as the crude tanker Gem No.2, was hit on 9 October during a surge of ship attacks in the region, which Iran is reported to have carried out. Satellite imagery indicates the slick had moved more than 35 km from the ship by Wednesday. UAE authorities say containment efforts have begun, while researchers say the full environmental damage is still too early to assess.

The spill is moving toward Siniyah and Khor Al Beidah islands, a recognised biodiversity area home to corals, seagrasses and endangered species such as green turtles and Halavi guitarfish.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by BBC News, Al Jazeera, The National, Middle East Eye.

headline: Kyiv says Starlink access restored as strikes continue on both sides
body:
What happened: Ukraine's defence minister, Yevhenii Khmara, said restrictions on military use of Starlink and Starshield satellite links have been lifted after more than a week of disruption that hit drone operations. He credited talks with Washington and President Zelenskyy's diplomacy, though it remains unclear who imposed the limits; US President Donald Trump denied responsibility. Separately, negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US are expected to meet in Abu Dhabi in early November. Strikes continued in Ukraine and Russia, with several deaths reported on both sides.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by BBC News, The Guardian, Ukrainska Pravda, Euronews.

headline: Israel seals off Hebron area and begins demolitions after deadly checkpoint attack
body:
What happened: Two Israeli soldiers were killed and three wounded at a checkpoint outside Hebron in the occupied West Bank, after two Palestinian gunmen opened fire. Both attackers were shot dead. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the military would destroy the neighbourhood the attackers came from, and Israeli forces have started demolishing Palestinian buildings there. Netanyahu also cordoned off Hebron and the nearby city of Halhul, and said plans for a large West Bank operation had been reviewed, without giving a date. The attack comes days before Israel's general election.

Reported by: AP. Also covered by Reuters, BBC News, Al Jazeera, The Guardian.

headline: Syrians rally against Israeli incursions in south, after deadly shooting in Daraa
body:
What happened: Demonstrations took place across Syria on Friday, protesting repeated Israeli incursions into the south, including one this week in Daraa province in which a man with a disability was reported killed by Israeli fire. Rallies were held in Damascus, Homs and Daraa city, with participants waving national flags and carrying slogans of solidarity. Syrian state media also reported Israeli forces advancing in Quneitra province and blocking roads, while the family of a man seized by Israel called for his release. Israel has said it will keep troops in a southern Syrian security zone.

The article notes that Israeli forces have also bulldozed olive groves, set up checkpoints and detained residents since the new Syrian government took power in December 2024, and that Israel has sent troops into the UN-patrolled buffer zone on the Golan Heights.

Reported by: Middle East Eye. Also covered by Al-Monitor, Press TV, Jerusalem Post.

headline: Ship attacks in Hormuz region hit record monthly high in October
body:
What happened: A Washington think tank tracking maritime incidents says October recorded more attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and nearby waters than any month since its records began in 2017. Its analyst counted 28 attacks in October and 113 since the Iran war started on February 28, with most of the September and October incidents concentrated in the strait. The International Maritime Organisation's tally of 120 incidents in the region broadly matches this, and it lists more than 30 supertankers damaged, 11 of them in October. Maritime monitors add that underreporting by shippers means the true picture is likely incomplete.

Reported by: Middle East Eye. Also covered by Reuters, Al Jazeera, Al-Monitor, Africanews.

headline: US tightens Middle East security over reported Iranian plots against Americans
body:
What happened: US intelligence reportedly warned that Iran is advancing plans to target American personnel overseas, with some plots said to be at an advanced stage in the Middle East and other regions. Citing a memo from the director of national intelligence, reported by Axios and the New York Times, officials said threats to US officials, including ambassadors, had been assessed in recent weeks, and that some Iranian operatives may already be active inside the United States. In response, Washington has reduced staff at several diplomatic missions in the region, including Saudi Arabia, amid wider concern over Iran-backed Houthi attacks and a possible renewed US-Israeli military campaign against Iran. Tehran has not publicly responded to the memo.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by Reuters, AP, France 24, Middle East Eye.

headline: Saudi coalition says it downed Houthi missiles over Riyadh and Khamis Mushait
body:
What happened: Saudi Arabia's coalition in Yemen said it intercepted and destroyed two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh and Khamis Mushait, along with two drones heading toward the southern region. The coalition's spokesperson, Major General Turki Al-Malki, also rejected Houthi claims that Riyadh had threatened tribal and civilian gatherings, calling them baseless and an effort to mislead the public and drag Yemeni tribes into the conflict. The report notes a later announcement of further interceptions, including missiles aimed at Taif and Yanbu, and a meeting between the Saudi and Pakistani foreign ministers on regional developments, particularly Yemen.

Reported by: Asharq Al-Awsat. Also covered by Middle East Eye, The National, Xinhua.

headline: Saudi and Pakistani ministers denounce Houthi missile attacks at Istanbul meeting
body:
What happened: On the sidelines of a Quadrilateral Group foreign ministers' meeting in Istanbul, Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan met his Pakistani counterpart Mohammad Ishaq Dar. The two sides condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi civilian areas, reviewed bilateral ties, and discussed de-escalation and safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb. Separately, Saudi air defences said they intercepted several Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh, Taif, Yanbu and Khamis Mushait, plus drones. The Saudi-led coalition also rejected Houthi claims that Riyadh had threatened tribal gatherings in Yemen as baseless.

Reported by: Asharq Al-Awsat. Also covered by The New Arab, Al-Monitor, The National, Taipei Times.

headline: Kyiv residents describe nightly shelter life as Russian strikes on the capital grow
body:
What happened: Russian attacks on Kyiv have intensified, pushing the capital of about 4 million people toward front-line conditions, with some subway stations serving as overnight shelters. Local accounts include a 14-year-old killed by a drone strike on his apartment in September and a drone hitting a school in early October, where pupils were already sheltered. Kyiv's military administration reported 140 deaths in the city over the first eight months of 2026, against 172 for all of 2025. Attacks on warehouses have caused supermarket shortages, and emergency power outages have resumed. A September poll by the Kyiv International Institute of Sociology found 72% of residents ready to endure the war as long as needed.

Reported by: DW. Also covered by Reuters, Ukrainska Pravda.

headline: Iran reportedly plans to disrupt Gulf undersea cables if conflict returns
body:
What happened: Two senior Iranian security officials told Reuters that Tehran has drawn up detailed plans to target undersea communications cables in the Gulf should the United States and Israel attack Iran again. They gave few specifics on methods or locations, but one said Iran would try to block repairs to prolong outages, including internet disruption. Iran's Revolutionary Guards deputy political affairs head Yadollah Javani had earlier said seven major cables beneath the Strait of Hormuz could be targeted. Analysts cautioned that the global effect could be limited, since under 1% of international bandwidth passes through the strait. Neither the US State Department nor Iran's Foreign Ministry responded to requests for comment, and Gulf states had not commented.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by The New Arab, Middle East Eye, Al-Monitor, CNA.

headline: Romania accuses Russia after drone sinks cargo ship off Black Sea coast
body:
What happened: A cargo ship, the Khoryv, sank after a drone strike about 24 km off Romania's Constanta port, which Romanian and European officials blame on Russia. One crew member died and three are missing, with nine rescued, according to Romania's naval authority. The vessel was flagged in Comoros, carried Ukrainian and Azeri sailors, and was heading for the Sulina port on the Danube. Romania's president and prime minister condemned the attack, and NATO said it would send more patrol aircraft, radar and drones to the Black Sea. Russia had not publicly responded at the time of reporting.

The sinking follows several other drone strikes on commercial shipping off Romania and Bulgaria in recent weeks. Ukraine, Romania and Bulgaria have asked NATO to speed up surveillance of the region.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by AP, Al Jazeera, Politico Europe, Ukrainska Pravda.

headline: Austria expels four Russian diplomats over security concerns
body:
What happened: Austria's foreign ministry has ordered four Russian diplomats based in Vienna to leave the country, declaring them persona non grata. Three are attached to the Russian Embassy in Vienna and one belongs to Russia's delegation to the OSCE. The ministry said their activities were incompatible with their diplomatic status and cited intelligence gathered by security services, without giving further details. The report originated with the Austrian broadcaster ORF and was relayed by European Pravda. It follows Hungary's expulsion of ten Russian embassy staff in September, which prompted Moscow to retaliate against Hungarian diplomats.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by AP, Ukrainska Pravda, Daily Maverick, The Moscow Times.
